descriptor: Cross-Family Selective-Geometry Alignment, Model-Indexed Quotient Intersection, Regime-Boundary Stability & Whether Behavioral Selectivity Constitutes a Transportable Model Property
scientific_question: Does the evidence currently constitute behavioral selectivity as a transportable model property, rather than a model/task-specific regime?

formal_domain.S: set of technically evaluable models satisfying the frozen SELECTIVE_PROMOTE or PARTIAL_SELECTIVE_PROMOTE gate
formal_domain.cross_family_alignment: defined only if |S| >= 2 and S contains at least two model families
formal_domain.quotient_intersection: intersection of model-indexed behavioral quotients is defined only over constituted promoted geometries; an empty-domain intersection must not be treated as universal by vacuous truth

boundary_stability.metric: minimum number of six valid/null majority-group outcomes that must change to enter a promotion region, conditional on technical evaluability
boundary_stability.technical_gate: kept logically prior to behavioral phase coordinates
boundary_stability.no_imputation: FORMAT_OR_API_FAIL rows are not repaired, reclassified, or counted as scientific negatives/positives for promotion

frozen_rules.transportable_property: requires at least two technically evaluable promoted models from distinct model families plus nonempty aligned geometry support

authority: Finite-design constitution test only. Failure to constitute transportability is not evidence that transportability is impossible in other models or tasks.
